findings.what: The disk cache validity check compares a POINT size against a PIXEL size, so it rejects every cached file it ever wrote: `if (cached && (fabs(cached.size.width - side) > 0.5f || fabs(cached.size.height - side) > 0.5f)) cached = nil;`
findings.failure: TGMediaViewController.m:452 calls `loadWithFileId:... square:TGMediaTileSide * scale` = 75*2 = 150, so `side` is 150 pixels. TGDecodeSquareThumbnail (src/TGImageDecode.m:29) builds the thumb with `UIGraphicsBeginImageContextWithOptions(CGSizeMake(side, side), NO, 0)` - scale 0 means screen scale, i.e. 2 on the 4S - producing a UIImage of size 150x150 POINTS backed by 300x300 PIXELS. Line 149-151 writes that as `<fileId>_150.png`, a 300x300 pixel file. On the next appearance line 128 does `[UIImage imageWithContentsOfFile:cachePath]`; the filename has no `@2x` suffix so the image comes back with scale 1.0 and size 300x300 points. `fabs(300 - 150) = 150 > 0.5` -> `cached = nil`. The disk cache therefore has a 100% miss rate: every media tile re-issues a TDLib downloadFile, re-decodes, re-encodes a PNG and rewrites the identical file on every single scroll pass, forever, and the Caches directory grows without ever being read.
findings.fix: Compare in pixels, not points. Replace line 129 with `if (cached && (fabs(cached.size.width * cached.scale - side) > 0.5f || fabs(cached.size.height * cached.scale - side) > 0.5f)) cached = nil;`. Separately fix the double-scaling: `side` is already in pixels at the call site, so TGDecodeSquareThumbnail must not multiply by the screen scale again - pass 1.0f instead of 0 as the scale argument of UIGraphicsBeginImageContextWithOptions in src/TGImageDecode.m:29, and after `[UIImage imageWithContentsOfFile:]` re-wrap with `[UIImage imageWithCGImage:cached.CGImage scale:[UIScreen mainScreen].scale orientation:UIImageOrientationUp]` so the tile draws at the right size.

findings.what: The shared thumbnail NSCache is bounded by object COUNT, not bytes: `cache.countLimit = 96;` while the objects it holds are 300x300-pixel decoded UIImages.
findings.failure: Because of the double-scaling described in the previous finding, each cached media thumbnail is 300x300 RGBA = 360 KB resident (the tile only ever displays 75x75 points, i.e. 150x150 pixels, so 4x more than needed). 96 entries x 360 KB = ~34 MB of decoded bitmaps in a process whose total usable footprint on a 512 MB iPhone 4S is roughly 40-60 MB. Scrolling a chat's shared-media grid past ~96 tiles reaches that ceiling and the app is jetsammed by iOS 6 before the memory-warning observer at line 17-22 (which only fires on a warning, and only after the allocation already happened) can help.
findings.fix: Switch to a cost-based bound: drop `countLimit` and set `cache.totalCostLimit = 3 * 1024 * 1024;`, then pass the byte cost at both insertion sites (line 133 and line 152) with `[TGRemoteImageMemoryCache() setObject:img forKey:cacheKey cost:(NSUInteger)(CGImageGetHeight(img.CGImage) * CGImageGetBytesPerRow(img.CGImage))]`. Also decode at the real display size (see the TGImageDecode scale fix above) so each entry is 150x150 pixels / 90 KB rather than 360 KB.

findings.what: `NSString *cachePath = [self cachePathForKey:cacheKey];` runs on the main thread, and `cachePathForKey:` (lines 70-77) performs a filesystem mutation on every call: `[[NSFileManager defaultManager] createDirectoryAtPath:dir withIntermediateDirectories:YES attributes:nil error:nil]`.
findings.failure: `loadWithFileId:square:placeholder:forceFade:` is called once per tile from TGMediaGridCell.configureWithItems: inside -tableView:cellForRowAtIndexPath:, i.e. 4 times per row on the main thread while the grid is scrolling. Each call issues NSSearchPathForDirectoriesInDomains plus a mkdir syscall against the app container. On an iPhone 4S that is several milliseconds of blocking I/O per row, which shows up directly as dropped frames and jerky scrolling in Shared Media.
findings.fix: Hoist the directory creation out of the per-call path: add a `static NSString *TGRemoteImageCacheDir(void)` that resolves the Caches path and calls createDirectoryAtPath: inside a `dispatch_once`, and make `cachePathForKey:` a pure `[TGRemoteImageCacheDir() stringByAppendingPathComponent:[key stringByAppendingString:@".png"]]` with no FileManager call.

findings.what: The URL-loading API declared in the header is a silent no-op: `- (void)loadImage:(NSString *)__unused url filter:(NSString *)__unused filter placeholder:(UIImage *)placeholder forceFade:(bool)__unused forceFade { self.placeholderImage = placeholder; self.image = placeholder; }`. The companion `currentUrl` property (TGRemoteImageView.h:10) is never written or read anywhere in the tree, and `-tryFillCache:` (line 52) has no callers.
findings.failure: TGRemoteImageView.h:15-16 advertise `loadImage:filter:placeholder:` and its forceFade variant as image loaders. Any future caller that uses the header as written gets a view permanently stuck on the placeholder with no error, no callback and no way to tell loading failed - the exact class of bug that costs an hour to find because the method visibly exists and visibly runs. Only `loadWithFileId:square:placeholder:forceFade:` actually loads anything.
findings.fix: Delete both `loadImage:filter:placeholder:` overloads (lines 61-68) and their header declarations (TGRemoteImageView.h:15-16), delete the unused `currentUrl` property (TGRemoteImageView.h:10), and delete `-tryFillCache:` (lines 52-59) plus its declaration (TGRemoteImageView.h:13). If a URL loader is wanted later, add it then with a real implementation.

findings.what: The recognizer defaults to accepting both directions - `self.direction = TGSwipeGestureRecognizerDirectionLeft | TGSwipeGestureRecognizerDirectionRight;` - and the only call site, TGChatListViewController.m:220-222, never narrows it: `TGSwipeGestureRecognizer *swipe = [[TGSwipeGestureRecognizer alloc] initWithTarget:self action:@selector(swipeRecognised:)]; [self addGestureRecognizer:swipe];`
findings.failure: The chat-list swipe actions are a right-anchored panel: TGChatListViewController.m:layoutSwipeButtonsCollapsed lays the buttons out from `width - kSwipeEdgeDistance` leftwards and animates them in from the right edge. Because the recognizer accepts a rightward swipe too, dragging a chat row to the RIGHT (the natural gesture for 'go back' / 'dismiss') pops open the Delete/Mute panel from the opposite edge. On a delete-capable row that is one mis-swipe away from destructive UI appearing where the user did not ask for it.
findings.fix: At TGChatListViewController.m:220, after allocating the recognizer, add `swipe.direction = TGSwipeGestureRecognizerDirectionLeft;` before `[self addGestureRecognizer:swipe];`.

findings.what: Six classes in this area are compiled into the binary (Makefile lines 231-237) but are never referenced from any other translation unit: TGActionTableView (257 lines), TGLabel (101), TGDateLabel (138), TGHighlightImageView (17), TGHighlightTriggerLabel (16), and the concrete TGReusableView base class (11). A whole-tree grep for each class name outside its own .m/.h pair returns only the TGReusableView *protocol* adoptions and the `prepareForRecycle:(TGViewRecycler *)` signature - no `alloc`, no `[[TGActionTableView` , no `[[TGDateLabel`, no `[[TGLabel`, no `[[TGHighlight...`.
findings.failure: About 540 lines of Objective-C plus their metadata, method lists and selector strings are linked into an app running on a 512 MB device, and every future agent reading the tree has to work out whether TGLabel or plain UILabel is 'the' label class and whether TGActionTableView is the table the chat list uses (it is not - TGChatListViewController uses a plain UITableView). The TGViewRecycler API `-recycledCount:` (TGViewRecycler.m:79) is likewise never called.
findings.fix: Drop `src/TGActionTableView.m`, `src/TGLabel.m`, `src/TGDateLabel.m`, `src/TGHighlightImageView.m`, `src/TGHighlightTriggerLabel.m` and `src/TGReusableView.m` from APP_SRC_M in the Makefile (lines 231-237) and delete the files together with their headers; keep only `TGReusableView.h`'s *protocol* declaration, which TGViewRecycler, TGRemoteImageView and TGStickerTile do use, by moving the `@protocol TGReusableView` block into TGViewRecycler.h and deleting the `@interface TGReusableView : UIView` class. Also delete `-recycledCount:` from TGViewRecycler.h:9 and .m:79-85.

findings.what: The duplicate guard returns before the cleanup work: `if ([views indexOfObjectIdenticalTo:view] != NSNotFound) return;` sits at line 65, ahead of `[view prepareForRecycle:self]` (line 68) and `[view removeFromSuperview]` (line 70-71).
findings.failure: If the same view is handed to -recycleView: twice (it is already sitting in the pool), the second call leaves it installed in its superview and still holding its content/targets while it is simultaneously advertised as free. A later -dequeueReusableViewWithIdentifier: hands that still-parented view to a different cell, which re-parents it, silently blanking the region of the first cell. The original 2013 recycler (TelegraphKit/TGViewRecycler.m:51-73) had no such guard at all and always ran prepareForRecycle first; this reordering is a local regression, currently unreachable only because both call sites (TGStickerPanelView.m:752/816 and TGMediaViewController.m:416/440) clear their tracking collection right after recycling.
findings.fix: Move `[view prepareForRecycle:self]` and the `removeFromSuperview` block above the `indexOfObjectIdenticalTo:` check so the view is always detached and reset, and let the duplicate check only skip the final `[views addObject:view]`.

findings.what: `- (void)cancelLoading { self.cancelled = true; }` latches the flag permanently, and only `loadWithFileId:square:placeholder:forceFade:` (line 95) ever clears it - `prepareForReuse` (line 38), `prepareForRecycle:` (line 45) and `loadPlaceholder:` (line 161) all set it and never reset.
findings.failure: Any code path that calls -loadPlaceholder: (or the stub -loadImage:...) and then expects a later in-flight delivery to land gets nothing: the `me.cancelled` test in the `deliver` block at line 120 short-circuits forever. Today this is latent because the media grid always goes through loadWithFileId:, but the header exposes cancelLoading/loadPlaceholder as public API with no documented one-shot semantics.
findings.fix: Set `self.cancelled = false;` at the top of `-loadPlaceholder:` (after the cancelLoading call, line 161) and at the top of `-loadImage:filter:placeholder:forceFade:` if that method is kept, so `cancelled` is strictly per-load rather than per-lifetime.

findings.what: `[(id<TGAdvancedHighlightable>)target advancedSetHighlighted:highlighted];` casts an element of the untyped `targetViews` array to a protocol it was never checked against - the array is `@property (nonatomic, strong) NSArray *targetViews;` with no element type and no respondsToSelector: guard.
findings.failure: With `advanced == true`, any target in the array that implements only the required `TGHighlightable` -setHighlighted: (which is what every plain UIImageView/UILabel provides) raises `-[UIImageView advancedSetHighlighted:]: unrecognized selector sent to instance` and terminates the app the moment the row is touched. The class is currently uninstantiated so this is unreachable today, but it will fire the first time anyone wires it up with a mixed target array.
findings.fix: If the class is kept rather than deleted per the dead-code finding, guard the branch: `if (self.advanced && [target respondsToSelector:@selector(advancedSetHighlighted:)]) [(id<TGAdvancedHighlightable>)target advancedSetHighlighted:highlighted]; else [target setHighlighted:highlighted];`. Also call `[super setHighlighted:highlighted]` first - the current override swallows it, so the label's own highlightedTextColor never takes effect.

findings.what: Every cache-hit delivery runs a snapshot-based cross-dissolve: `[UIView transitionWithView:self duration:duration options:UIViewAnimationOptionTransitionCrossDissolve animations:^{ self.image = image; } completion:nil];`, and TGMediaTileView sets `self.fadeTransition = true` (TGMediaViewController.m:299) so `fade` is true for every tile.
findings.failure: UIViewAnimationOptionTransitionCrossDissolve makes UIKit render two offscreen snapshots of the view and blend them for the duration. During a Shared Media scroll, four tiles per row each start their own transition as their thumbnail arrives, so the single A5 core is compositing 8 extra offscreen surfaces per row on top of the decode work - measurable stutter on a 4S for a 0.14s effect nobody sees while scrolling.
findings.fix: Only fade when the view is not being filled during active scrolling: skip the transition when the previous contents were already a real image, e.g. `if (fade && self.image == self.placeholderImage) { ...transition... } else { self.image = image; }`, or expose a `suppressFade` flag that TGMediaViewController sets while `tableView.isDragging || tableView.isDecelerating`.
